title: Pythia: Compiler-Guided Defense Against Non-Control Data Attacks
problem: Modern C/C++ applications are vulnerable to Non-Control Data Attacks, particularly Control-flow Bending where adversaries manipulate program data to flip branch outcomes and divert control flow. Existing CFI mechanisms fail to defend against such attacks involving branch predicate manipulation.
motivation: Protecting applications from sophisticated non-control data attacks that bypass current state-of-the-art defenses is critical for system security.
method: Pythia works by having the compiler add monitoring code to your program that guards the data values used in branching decisions (the points where a program chooses between different execution paths). An attacker using a control-flow bending attack tries to corrupt this data to make the program execute incorrectly. Pythia's protective code detects when someone attempts to modify this critical data and blocks the modification before it takes effect. This stops attacks that traditional control-flow integrity measures miss, since those tools only protect where a program can jump to, not the conditions that decide whether to jump in the first place.
key_novelty: The single core idea is having the compiler automatically add protective monitoring of the data that controls program branches, catching corruption attempts before they can misdirect execution.
contributions: Identifies limitations of CFI mechanisms against control-flow bending attacks
Proposes compiler-guided defense for protecting branch predicates
Addresses non-control data attacks that alter control flow through data corruption
Extends defense beyond traditional control-flow integrity
